newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Korean, Japan petrochem companies to meet on price.
newsitem.headline: Korean, Japan petrochem companies to meet on price.

text.p: South Korean and Japanese petrochemical companies plan to hold an extraordinary meeting in Seoul on December 18 to discuss the high price of feedstock naphtha, industry sources said on Monday.

South Korean sources said the meeting would discuss broad issues, but was also a direct result of seven South Korean companies decision last week to temporarily suspend trade with Itochu Corp of Japan, which they accused of manipulating prices.
"We have regular meetings two times a year with Japanese and European end-users," said a source at South Korean petrochemical company.
But he said the two meetings have already taken place this year, in South Korea and in Germany.

"This time we will discuss how end-users cope with this kind of different situation, how to avoid manipulation made by the sellers' side and if possible, we want to make counter-measures against manipulation," he said.
Sources said there will be two representatives for the Japanese petrochemical companies, from Mitsubishi Chemical Corp and Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd.
But Japanese sources declined to comment on the meeting.
"Crude prices rose in a small range but naphtha prices have sky-rocketted artificially," said a naphtha buyer for a South Korean petrochemical company.
Traders said the differential or "crack" between Brent crude and Tokyo's forward open-specification (open-spec) contract was usually between $50-$60 per tonne.
Earlier in December, the prompt crack ballooned out to $76 per tonne, amid allegations of price manipulation in the open-spec market.
Since early last week, the crack has narrowed by more than $12 to $64 on Monday.
